> **What this case shows** — the ACF, PACF and AR folds all *described* the EEG's temporal structure;
> the **Ljung-Box test** *tests* it. It aggregates the first *h* squared autocorrelations into a single
> statistic **Q** and asks: could this be white noise? This case adds the test (**`ljungBoxTest`**,
> built on the ACF). On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces
> **`statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.acorr_ljungbox`** **bit-for-bit** — statistic *and* p-value — and the
> answer is emphatic: **Q = 4165, about 228× the 95% threshold**, so the white-noise null is rejected
> overwhelmingly.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `ljungBoxTest(x, lag)` → the Q statistic, p-value and df.
**Way of thinking** — a description ("the ACF decays slowly") becomes a decision ("not white noise,
p < 0.001") through a test. Ljung-Box is that test; on *residuals* it flips to a model-adequacy check —
a Q *below* the threshold says your model has whitened the signal.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::ljungBoxTest()`, built on `autocorrelation()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `ljungBoxTest` reproduces `statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.acorr_ljungbox`
bit-for-bit for both the Q statistic and the p-value; at h=10, Q=4165 is ~228× the 95% chi-square
critical value (18.31), so the white-noise null is rejected.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a decision: the ecosystem had no formal autocorrelation test — can we author
the Ljung-Box portmanteau test, reproduce statsmodels exactly, and quantify how decisively eyes-closed
EEG departs from white noise?** The goal is to introduce `ljungBoxTest`, certify it bit-for-bit, and
report the margin.

## Challenge & approach

The Ljung-Box statistic is Q = N(N+2)·Σ_{k=1}^{h} ρ̂_k²/(N−k), built from the ACF (via
`autocorrelation`), with a chi-square(h) reference distribution under the white-noise null. We compute
Q and its p-value and check them against `statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.acorr_ljungbox` on the identical
signal.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → ACF (lags 1..10) → Q = N(N+2)·Σ ρ_k²/(N−k) → p = chi²(10) upper tail
                    vs statsmodels.acorr_ljungbox (same signal) → bit-exact (|diff| 0) for Q and p
                    Q = 4165 vs critical 18.31 → 228× over → reject white noise (p ≈ 0)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[autocorrelation](../autocorrelation-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [PACF](../pacf-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and
[AR](../ar-yule-walker-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the cumulative Ljung-Box Q as more lags are included (log scale, red) against the matching 95% chi-square threshold (green dashed) — Q sits orders of magnitude above the threshold from the first lag. Right: the final Q (4165) versus the 95% critical value (18.31) on a log scale — a ~228× margin.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel shows the statistic overshooting the threshold at every lag; the
right panel is the verdict — Q dwarfs the critical value, so the signal is decisively not white noise.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Ljung-Box Q** (h = 10) | **4165** |
| Q vs `statsmodels` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-exact) |
| p-value vs `statsmodels` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-exact) |
| 95% chi-square critical value (10 df) | **18.31** |
| white-noise null rejected | **yes** |
| Q as a multiple of critical | **228×** |

The newly-authored op equals statsmodels for both the statistic and the p-value, and the verdict is
unambiguous. Values trace to
[`artifacts/ljungbox_summary.csv`](artifacts/ljungbox_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`ljungBoxTest` adds the formal counterpart to the descriptive ACF/PACF/AR lane, and it is exact:
bit-for-bit against statsmodels for both the statistic and the p-value. The transferable takeaway:
**describe with the ACF, decide with Ljung-Box. On a raw signal it confirms there is structure to model;
on your model's residuals it tells you whether you have captured it — a residual Q under the threshold is
the certificate that the model whitened the data.**

## Open questions

- The test is most useful on model residuals: running it on the residuals of the folded `arYuleWalker`
  fit would test whether the AR(4) model has whitened the EEG (a residual Q below critical would confirm
  adequacy). *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Ljung-Box white-noise / adequacy test | `ljungBoxTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Autocorrelation | `autocorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| AR fit (residuals to test) | `arYuleWalker()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **lag** — the number of autocorrelations to pool, and the chi-square degrees of freedom (default 10);
  too few misses long-range structure, too many dilutes power. For AR residuals, use lag > model order.
- **interpretation** — a large Q / small p means autocorrelation is present (raw signal) or the model is
  inadequate (residuals); a small Q / large p means the series is consistent with white noise.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

lb <- ljungBoxTest(x, lag = 10)
lb$statistic; lb$p_value            # Q and its chi-square p-value
lb$statistic > qchisq(0.95, lb$df)  # reject white noise at 5%?
# reproduces statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.acorr_ljungbox bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/ljungbox_summary.csv`](artifacts/ljungbox_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
the Q statistic, the bit-exact statsmodels match for both statistic and p-value, the 95% critical value,
the rejection and its margin, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op built on autocorrelation;
machine-precision; decisive-but-expected verdict; residual-adequacy use).
